technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment as extensions to the existing Spring XD module, stream, task, UI, and class-loading extension points rather than redesigning the platform.
Use configurable Kafka serializer and deserializer components, exposed through module properties and applied consistently to Kafka source, sink, and bus endpoints.
Implement the gpfdist sink as an out-of-the-box stream sink module using the gpfdist wire protocol and configurable target host, port, table or file settings, batching, and retry behavior.

Provide UI infrastructure as shared backend and frontend integration scaffolding, including module registration, service endpoints, navigation or extension hooks, and the minimum build configuration needed by admin_ui and Flo.

Use a tasklet-based approach for bulk file and gpload operations so large files are streamed or transferred in bounded buffers instead of being represented as individual messages or retained fully in memory.
Implement gpload as a task module that generates or invokes GPDB/HAWQ loading operations, validates configuration, handles process results, and reports task success or failure.
Remove Hadoop libraries from the root runtime classpath and load Hadoop-dependent functionality only when required by the module registry or a module's execution configuration.

Implement dynamic module classpaths with property expansion, glob support, module-specific and distribution-specific locations, explicit custom paths, deterministic classpath ordering, and isolated child class loaders where required.
Preserve backward compatibility for existing module configurations and provide fallback behavior when new classpath or codec properties are absent.
Use automated unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, with performance-oriented checks for Kafka throughput, large-file processing, and classpath startup behavior.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD codebase, build system, module abstractions, Kafka integration, task framework, and deployment packaging are available and buildable.

The increment is implemented by one software developer, and effort includes design, coding, code review preparation, testing, debugging, documentation, and packaging work, but not elapsed calendar time.
Existing Kafka, GPDB/HAWQ, gpfdist, gpload, Hadoop, admin_ui, and Flo environments or test doubles can be used; creating or operating production infrastructure is excluded.
The exact versions of Kafka, GPDB/HAWQ, Hadoop distributions, and UI frameworks are selected to match the versions already supported by the repository.

The gpfdist sink and gpload tasklet only need to support the formats, authentication mechanisms, and operational options exposed by the existing Spring XD conventions; novel database features are excluded.
UI infrastructure means integration scaffolding and extension points for admin_ui and Flo, not complete administration screens or a full visual flow designer.

The end-to-end Kafka use case includes one representative scalable producer-to-Spring-XD-to-consumer flow, deployment configuration, repeatable test data, and performance instrumentation, not a production-grade benchmark suite.
Backward compatibility is required for existing Kafka modules, task definitions, module registry behavior, and deployments where Hadoop is present on the existing classpath.
Security hardening, multi-tenant isolation, extensive documentation redesign, and long-term maintenance after delivery are outside the estimate.
Effort values are most-likely estimates and include normal integration troubleshooting for the stated scope.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing module, stream, task, Kafka, UI, class-loading, build, and packaging implementations; map each user story to extension points; define configuration and compatibility boundaries.

Design and implement configurable serializer and deserializer selection for Kafka source, sink, and bus components; add property binding, defaults, validation, error handling, backward compatibility, and focused unit tests.

Implement the gpfdist sink module, including protocol handling, stream buffering, configurable connection and target settings, retry and failure behavior, module metadata, packaging, and unit or integration tests.

activities.activity_name: UI infrastructure for admin_ui and Flo
activities.activity_description: Add the backend APIs, module metadata, frontend build or integration configuration, registration hooks, navigation or extension points, and developer documentation required for admin_ui and Flo integration.

Create a representative scalable Kafka and Spring XD flow with deployment configuration, sample data generation and consumption, operational instructions, repeatable validation, instrumentation, and troubleshooting of the complete path.

Design and implement bounded-buffer or streaming file processing through the task framework, avoiding line-by-line message retention and full-file memory usage; add configuration, restart or failure behavior, and large-file tests.

Implement the gpload tasklet, including task configuration, source and manifest handling, GPDB/HAWQ invocation or integration, process output and exit-code handling, validation, cleanup, packaging, and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Remove Hadoop dependencies from the root classpath
activities.activity_description: Identify root-level Hadoop dependencies and transitive loading paths; refactor dependency declarations and startup initialization; preserve HDFS-backed registry behavior through conditional loading; add startup and compatibility tests.

Implement module-specific class-loader construction, property expansion, distribution and provider substitution, wildcard path resolution, explicit custom classpath support, classpath ordering, diagnostics, isolation, and configuration tests.

activities.activity_name: Cross-feature automated testing and regression fixes
activities.activity_description: Add or extend unit, integration, packaging, compatibility, negative-path, and regression tests across Kafka codecs, gpfdist, tasklets, Hadoop decoupling, dynamic classpaths, and UI infrastructure; diagnose and fix discovered defects.

Run the complete increment in representative local or CI environments; validate Kafka throughput, large-file memory behavior, GPDB/HAWQ loading, optional Hadoop startup, dynamic dependency resolution, and end-to-end module interoperability.

Document configuration properties, deployment prerequisites, examples, operational limitations, migration behavior, and the Kafka demonstration; update build and distribution artifacts and prepare the increment for delivery.
